names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 1 Μαρτίου, «Αγία Αναστασία η Νεομάρτυς», with the rank word left off. The body of the page adds a patronymic in brackets and in Greek letters, «της Ρωσίδας Αγίας Αναστασίας (Αντρέγιεβνα)»; that bracketed form is the site's own rendering of a Russian word and is kept in the display name rather than stored as a name form.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding menologion day (30 September 2026). saint.gr calls her Russian, so that calendar is the one most likely to hold her, and it was not read.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 1ης Μαρτίου — «Αγία Αναστασία η Νεομάρτυς»

attestations.note: The page is one sentence and it is a statement of what the site does not know: «Δεν έχουμε λεπτομέρειες για τον βίο και το Μαρτύριο της Ρωσίδας Αγίας Αναστασίας (Αντρέγιεβνα) παρά μόνο ότι ήταν διά Χριστόν σαλή» — we have no details of the life and martyrdom of the Russian saint Anastasia (Andreyevna) except that she was a fool for Christ. It gives no year at all, no place in Russia, no relic, no distich and no hymn.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding menologion day (30 September 2026).
